findings.text: rederived_section_fields calls section_derivation(read, section) with derive_write_paths left at its default True, so the new described-test resolution also runs on the release path: an entry that supplied its own write paths but took the section's done_when is marked only on done_when (derive_write_paths is used at :591 only), and a section whose sentence describes a test whose done-when names zero or two tests/ files now raises there, which reviews.py:718 turns into _RederivationRefusedError and a held request. That contradicts the plan deliverable's 'An entry that gives its own write paths ... are unchanged' and the commit message's claim that such an entry is never asked for the derivation, and it newly holds requests queued before this change whose write paths were derived from such a sentence.

_batch() gives every entry no write_paths field, so the exemption added at reckon/crew/dispatch_batch.py:591 (derive_write_paths=not write_paths) is reached by no test; deleting that argument and always deriving would leave the suite green while refusing entries that supply their own paths.

_described_test_path extracts tests/ paths from prose with its own startswith('tests/') and suffix test rather than extending reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py:688, which owns _TEST_PATH_PATTERN for the same job; the two now accept different sets (any suffixed file versus *.py), so a later change to one will not reach the other.
